summary.text: The carbonate compensation depth is the ocean depth at which calcium carbonate dissolves as fast as it is supplied from above.
Below it, the carbonate shells of plankton dissolve instead of being preserved, so carbonate particles cannot build up on deeper seafloor.
Its depth depends on temperature, pressure and dissolved CO₂, and today it ranges from about 4200 m in parts of the Pacific to about 5000 m in the Atlantic.

items.prompt: An undersea plateau rises above the carbonate compensation depth, while a nearby trench floor lies well below it. Where would you expect chalky carbonate ooze?
items.explain: Seabed above the CCD can collect calcareous ooze, but below it the tiny shells dissolve before they can settle.

items.prompt: Deep water gathers more dissolved CO₂ the longer it stays away from the surface. Where would the CCD sit in the oldest water masses?
items.explain: Older water holds more CO₂, which makes calcium carbonate more soluble, so the oldest water masses have the shallowest CCD.

items.prompt: Aragonite, another form of calcium carbonate, dissolves more readily than calcite. Where does its compensation depth generally lie?

options.label: At the same depth as calcite's

items.explain: Because aragonite is more soluble than calcite, the aragonite compensation depth is generally shallower.

items.prompt: People keep burning fossil fuels and CO₂ in the air keeps climbing. What is that doing to the carbonate compensation depth?
items.explain: Rising atmospheric CO₂ from fossil fuels is causing the CCD to rise, with downwelling zones affected first.

items.prompt: As a seafloor plate spreads away from where it formed, it cools and sinks to greater depth. What can happen to a carbonate layer laid down on it earlier?

options.label: It is lifted above sea level
It can end up below the CCD
It melts back into the mantle

items.explain: Thermal subsidence deepens the seafloor and may carry the carbonate layer below the CCD, though overlying sediments can slow its dissolving.

items.prompt: On seafloor lying well below the carbonate compensation depth, what kind of ooze is most common?
items.explain: Below the CCD carbonate dissolves, so siliceous ooze, mostly radiolarians and diatoms, is the most common ooze.
